description.value: Small user-maintained lakeshore campsite on Kitsumkalum Lake, reached via a short gravel road off the Nisga'a Highway 25 km north of Terrace; sandy beach for swimming and good paddling, but pit toilet only with no potable water — bring your own.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website for Kitsumkalum Park is fully accessible and serves as the primary evidence source. It explicitly states 'A pit toilet is the only facility provided' and 'Bring your own drinking water as potable water is not available in the park,' which drives the two confirmed amenity values. The OSM name 'Kalum Lake Campsite' differs from the BC Parks official name 'Kitsumkalum Park,' which is flagged as a concern; the lake itself is named Kitsumkalum Lake throughout the website.
concerns: Name mismatch: OSM records this as 'Kalum Lake Campsite' but the BC Parks website and the lake are both named 'Kitsumkalum' — likely a colloquial abbreviation rather than a distinct entity, but should be confirmed.
Extremely limited facilities (pit toilet only, no potable water) — cyclists must be fully self-sufficient; this should be clearly communicated in the listing.
No address, phone, or email in OSM; general BC Parks contact details (parkinfo@gov.bc.ca, 1-800-689-9025) are available on the contact subpage but are not park-specific.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, road-accessible BC Parks campsite on the Nisga'a Highway corridor in a region with very few cycling services; despite minimal facilities it is a viable overnight stop for touring cyclists and merits a listing with clear facility caveats.
enrichment_extras.notes: The campground accommodates up to seven small camping parties and is user-maintained. Bears (black and grizzly) are commonly seen; cyclists should take appropriate bear-safety precautions. Reservation status for this specific user-maintained site is not confirmed on the website.

wow_evidence: sandy beach for swimming and good paddling
